what: The community Lean proof (platypii/integer-mult-bounds-lean at aaf10926: integer multiplication in O(n (log n)^(1 − κ)) steps on a multi-stack Turing machine, κ = 4222422970/2^46) against the statement file of the same repository, MathlibTM2/Statement.lean. The statement is the repository's own: this checks that the theorem mulInTime proves exactly that proposition, on the three standard axioms, under a second kernel, and that the check refuses statements we changed. Whether the proposition is OpenAI's theorem is a reading, kept apart.

canonical.what: the repository's own statement file: one fixed multi-stack machine multiplies two binary naturals in worst-case time O(n (log n)^(1 − κ)), n the input length, with Mathlib's asymptotic notation over the reals

claim.what: the theorem with the explicit saving; the existential statement of the same file follows from it in one line
claim.license: MIT (the repository's); no byte of the file is kept here but its declaration's header

f3.what: the statement is an existence claim with no hypotheses to satisfy

theorem mulInTime : MulInTime (4222422970 / 2 ^ 46 : ℝ) :=

f2NotApplicable: the statement quantifies over Turing machines and has no decidable instance to evaluate; the encodings it names are evaluated on small pairs by a separate check of the same audit
notInScope: the mathematics beyond what the kernel checks; whether a multi-stack machine's time is a multitape machine's time; the statement does not require finite work-stack alphabets (Mathlib's FinTM2 requires it of the input stack only), which is read and argued apart; the constant hidden in the O
